title: Creating and Managing Directories
learning_outcomes: Describe Creating directories and explain how it relates to Creating and Managing Directories.
Demonstrate Recursive directory creation in a small Node.js example and predict the observable result.
Test a failure, boundary, lifecycle, or version-compatibility case involving Listing directory contents.

content.intro: Creating and Managing Directories is part of file system operations. This lesson connects Creating directories, Recursive directory creation, Listing directory contents to a concrete Node.js example. Focus on the behavior you can observe, the assumptions the API makes, and one failure or boundary case.
content.why_it_matters: The filesystem APIs operate on paths and bytes, and asynchronous operations avoid blocking the JavaScript thread while I/O is pending. Test missing files, permission failures, empty files, large inputs, and path traversal attempts.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: The filesystem APIs operate on paths and bytes, and asynchronous operations avoid blocking the JavaScript thread while I/O is pending. Prefer promise-based async I/O for application workflows, validate paths, handle expected errors, and stream large files.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety note
content_blocks.text: Teaching baseline: use a supported Node.js LTS release (Node.js 24 LTS as checked on 2026-10-13). The official releases page lists Node.js 26 as Current and Node.js 24/22 as LTS. Some advanced APIs, flags, permission behavior, embedded SQLite capabilities, module-loader hooks, and TypeScript integration are version-sensitive; verify the exact installed runtime. The Node.js 22 runtime available in the build-check environment is used only for syntax checks. This example is for learning and static validation, not for executing untrusted learner code inside CodeLeaf.

content.task: Create or inspect a small Node.js example for Creating and Managing Directories. Include at least one listed subtopic, document the expected result, and verify a normal case plus a boundary or failure case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates a named lesson concept, rather than only mentioning the title.
Expected output or observable behavior is documented and reproducible.
At least one invalid, empty, timeout, resource, or failure case is handled or explained.
The solution does not put secrets in source code and does not execute untrusted code inside the production API process.

common_mistakes.problem: Concatenating untrusted filenames into paths or loading an arbitrarily large file into memory.
common_mistakes.why: The code may pass a simple demonstration yet fail with real inputs, resource limits, timing, or runtime differences.
common_mistakes.fix: Resolve paths under an approved directory, enforce size limits, and use streams where appropriate.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a snippet without checking its runtime, dependencies, input assumptions, or cleanup behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Node.js APIs and surrounding ecosystem tools have explicit version, trust, and resource boundaries.
common_mistakes.fix: State the environment and dependency assumptions, then rerun the example from a clean starting state.
